entries.what: The reference row showed a score of 68.7 with 3 hangs and 42 skipped checks (coverage 60.4). A reference compared with its own recording scores 100; anything less is a measurement error.

entries.what: Types and bulk counts charged one gap many times. SereneDB's types role showed 222 different answers; 114 of them were one refusal of DECLARE (42601), recorded by the binary cursor check and again by each of 113 per-type binary cursor checks. Per-type checks also repeated the refusal of their own type's check (text parameters, COPY per type), per-type COPY checks counted as not matching when the COPY format itself was refused, and per-type binary cursor checks counted as matching on types the engine refuses, because the cursor and the engine's own query refused them alike. Types, bulk or overall scores of these rows move by 1 point or more: up for cockroachdb, serenedb, cedardb, doltgres, materialize, duckgres, ydb and greptimedb; down for cratedb, questdb, risingwave, arcadedb, clickhouse and picodata; spanner-pg types down and bulk up.
entries.cause_detail: A foundation check that the engine refused with a server error the reference did not have still counted as working where any usable answer was enough, so every check built on it ran and recorded the same refusal. Checks that repeat one mechanism for every value type counted as not matching when the mechanism or the type was missing, instead of being left out with the gap counted once where it is measured.
entries.fix_title: Count a refused feature once, where it is measured
entries.note: v0.1.3 (45a7361f915b) was measured with the fix. There, SereneDB's refused DECLARE (42601) is charged once, by the new cursor check, and the binary cursor check and its 167 per-type checks are left out of the score; SereneDB's types role has 128 of 246 judged checks matched. No per-type COPY check of these rows counts as not matching for a refused COPY format, and no per-type binary cursor check counts as matching on a type the engine refuses. A repeat this fix alone left, a table column of a type the engine refuses charged again in every per-type COPY format (v0.1.2: CockroachDB 30 checks, Duckgres 36, SereneDB 8), is left out by 173271b284d550f45405703250466ebbd7a423a8 Count a refused column of a type once, under types, also part of v0.1.3: 36 such checks on Duckgres and 9 on CockroachDB, the others with their type's own check. One known repeat of 2 checks remains in v0.1.3, on ArcadeDB: its cursor checks are left out for the :: cast (E9), while the binary cursor checks of NULL and of an untyped literal send no :: and run, and each records ArcadeDB's 42601 at DECLARE. It does not change ArcadeDB's types score, which is 0.0 with or without them. Made after v0.1.3, 67fbd6617851cd0f4e42cdf7eddd9d386a2b145c Count a refused cursor once on an engine that also refuses :: corrects it: the cursor checks send no :: and compare the cursor with the same engine's result of the same query, so a refused DECLARE is charged once, by the cursor check, and the binary cursor checks of NULL and of an untyped literal are left out with the other checks built on the cursor. In v0.1.3 ArcadeDB answered DECLARE with 42601 for both of those cursors; if it answers the cursor check's DECLARE the same way, its types role has 0 of 5 judged checks matched instead of 0 of 6, and no score of the row changes. The first dataset measured with it is the next release. Scores, v0.1.2 published to v0.1.3 measured (frames, types, bulk, overall): CockroachDB 63.9 to 63.4, 36.1 to 58.3, 44.5 to 84.7, 50.0 to 68.2; SereneDB 58.3 to 57.9, 31.6 to 52.0, 46.2 to 80.0, 46.9 to 62.7; CedarDB 55.6 to 60.0, 42.8 to 62.2, 9.0 to 12.1, 38.1 to 46.6; Doltgres 50.0 to 50.0, 46.5 to 66.2, 2.3 to 82.7, 34.9 to 64.4; Materialize 44.4 to 44.7, 20.9 to 43.1, 0.1 to 1.2, 24.5 to 31.4; Duckgres 27.8 to 32.5, 16.0 to 24.6, 14.3 to 44.7, 20.4 to 33.8; YDB 16.7 to 18.4, 26.5 to 46.1, 0.1 to 1.2, 14.7 to 21.5; GreptimeDB 19.4 to 21.1, 9.0 to 14.4, 0.3 to 1.2, 10.7 to 13.3; Spanner PG 13.9 to 13.2, 33.7 to 9.8, 1.2 to 7.3, 16.0 to 10.5; CrateDB 30.6 to 31.6, 28.9 to 24.2, 0.0 to 0.0, 21.1 to 20.1; QuestDB 25.0 to 26.3, 30.7 to 9.9, 0.0 to 0.0, 19.3 to 13.7; RisingWave 22.2 to 23.7, 32.3 to 28.4, 0.0 to 0.0, 18.6 to 18.1; ArcadeDB 19.4 to 36.8, 31.9 to 0.0, 0.0 to 0.0, 17.4 to 15.2; ClickHouse 8.3 to 10.5, 29.7 to 0.0, 0.0 to 0.0, 12.2 to 4.3; Picodata 5.6 to 7.9, 29.5 to 12.7, 0.0 to 0.0, 11.0 to 7.0. A v0.1.3 number also reflects the other changes between the two releases, not this fix alone: new checks (TLS and the :: cast check in frames, jsonb in types and bulk, COPY cases split into checks of their own), per-type COPY checks that compare COPY with the same engine instead of with the reference, detection fixes, and the other errata here. entries.what: These engines answer the extended query foundation (SELECT $1::int4) with a server error (ArcadeDB 42601, ClickHouse 2F000, Spanner PG P0001), and the 10 extended query and pipeline checks built on it ran anyway instead of being skipped with the gap counted once: 9 of them were charged on ArcadeDB, 10 on ClickHouse and 9 on Spanner PG, several with the same error code. The per-type text parameter checks of these rows ran on the same foundation.
entries.cause_detail: The foundation kept the server error only in its frames unless its code meant unsupported, so the refusal was not seen and the capability counted as working.
entries.fix_title: Record a pgwire foundation's refusal where the runner sees it
entries.note: v0.1.3 (45a7361f915b) was measured with the fix. On ClickHouse and Spanner PG the 10 extended query and pipeline checks are skipped there and count against the row, with the gap charged once, at the foundation, and the text parameter checks that need it are left out of the score (18 and 40). Close statement and portal, which matched on Spanner PG, is skipped with the rest. On ArcadeDB the foundation sends SELECT $1::int4 and is left out of the score like every frames check that sends :: because E9 charges ArcadeDB's 42601 for :: once, at the :: cast check. Of its dependents, Close statement and portal and Execute row limit send no :: and run: Close matches as in v0.1.2, and Execute row limit answers with XX000 where the reference succeeds. Frames went from 7 of 36 judged checks matched to 7 of 19 on ArcadeDB, 3 of 36 to 4 of 38 on ClickHouse and 5 of 36 to 5 of 38 on Spanner PG: the new TLS session and :: cast checks add 2 judged checks to each row, the cast check matches on ClickHouse and Spanner PG, and 19 ArcadeDB checks are left out for the cast. Scores, v0.1.2 published to v0.1.3 measured (frames, types, bulk, overall): ArcadeDB 19.4 to 36.8, 31.9 to 0.0, 0.0 to 0.0, 17.4 to 15.2; ClickHouse 8.3 to 10.5, 29.7 to 0.0, 0.0 to 0.0, 12.2 to 4.3; Spanner PG 13.9 to 13.2, 33.7 to 9.8, 1.2 to 7.3, 16.0 to 10.5. The types and bulk moves come from E4, E9 and other changes between the releases, not from this fix. Every row named here ran the same image digest in both releases.

entries.what: One refused cast syntax was charged once per check that sends it. Every typed case of the types table, and the binary cursor and text parameter checks of each, send their values with PostgreSQL's :: cast, and frames checks pin their literals with it (SELECT 1::int4, SELECT $1::int4). ArcadeDB answers '1'::int4 with 42601: 336 types checks were charged for it, and of the 19 frames checks that send :: 16 were counted as different and 3 as skipped. ClickHouse answers both forms the array cases cast with, ARRAY[...]::<type>[] and '{...}'::<type>[], with 2F000 where 'a'::text works, and 134 array checks were charged for it. 160 and 64 checks of these rows counted as matching because the engine failed both paths they compare alike, and the per-type COPY checks built on these cases (648 and 264) were skipped and counted as not matching.
entries.cause_detail: Nothing probed the cast syntax on its own, so each check that sends it recorded the same refusal, and the audit listed the cluster for review instead of finding it.
entries.fix_title: Count a refused :: cast once, at a cast foundation
entries.note: v0.1.3 (45a7361f915b) was measured with this fix and with 6871677c028924ed5575409a96cde5f65f301923 Count a refused :: once across the row, and gate only on forms sent, which completes it: the :: cast check runs right after startup and every check that sends :: needs it, and the array cast counts as refused only when both forms the array checks send fail where the element's cast works. On ArcadeDB the 42601 is charged once across the row, at the :: cast check in frames; the 19 frames checks, 499 types checks and 576 bulk checks that send :: are left out of the score. On ClickHouse the :: cast check matches, and its 2F000 for both array forms (ARRAY['a'::text]::text[] and '{}'::text[], where 'a'::text works) is charged once, at the array cast check; 198 array types checks and 257 array bulk checks are left out. CrateDB and Picodata answer ARRAY['a'::text]::text[], so their array cast check matches and their array checks are judged on their own answers, as in v0.1.2. Spanner PG answers CAST('1' AS int4) with the same P0001 as '1'::int4, so its :: cast check matches and the refusal stays counted per type. ArcadeDB's frames role has 7 of 19 judged checks matched (7 of 36 in v0.1.2) and its types role 0 of 6; ClickHouse's frames role 4 of 38 and its types role 0 of 96. Scores, v0.1.2 published to v0.1.3 measured (frames, types, bulk, overall): ArcadeDB 19.4 to 36.8, 31.9 to 0.0, 0.0 to 0.0, 17.4 to 15.2; ClickHouse 8.3 to 10.5, 29.7 to 0.0, 0.0 to 0.0, 12.2 to 4.3. A v0.1.3 number also reflects the other changes between the two releases, not this fix alone: new checks (TLS and the :: cast check in frames, jsonb in types and bulk, COPY cases split into checks of their own), per-type COPY checks that compare COPY with the same engine instead of with the reference, detection fixes, and the other errata here. Every row named here ran the same image digest in both releases.

entries.what: On these engines SELECT 1::int4 AS slept FROM pg_sleep(5), the query the cancel checks interrupt, returned within milliseconds, one gap, and each cancel check that needed it running counted it. SereneDB was charged in 4 checks: CancelRequest during pg_sleep and pg_cancel_backend were skipped ("the sleep was not executed"), CancelRequest with a key that does not match was skipped for want of the first, and pg_terminate_backend differed because the query finished before it could be ended. RisingWave was charged in 2: pg_cancel_backend was skipped the same way and pg_terminate_backend differed.
entries.cause_detail: No check measured whether pg_sleep waits, so the gap had no check of its own to be counted in, and each check that needed a sleeping query counted it again.
entries.fix_title: Charge a pg_sleep that does not wait once, at a sleep check
entries.note: Not yet re-measured; v0.1.3 was measured without the fix, and the next dataset is the first measured with it. The new check pgwire.frame.cancel.sleep counts the gap once, as "pg_sleep(1) in a FROM clause returns without sleeping", and the four checks above are not applicable on these rows. On RisingWave, CancelRequest during pg_sleep and with a key that does not match were skipped in v0.1.2 because the engine sends no BackendKeyData, which the startup check already counts; they are not applicable as well. CancelRequest during COPY TO is not part of this gap and keeps its v0.1.2 counts: on SereneDB it matched, its COPY with pg_sleep(0.1) per row still running when the cancel arrived; on RisingWave it was skipped for want of COPY from a query. It is weighed by the sleep check only when its COPY completes before the cancel arrives.

entries.what: The 7 pgwire.am.copy.* checks (copy.in-text, copy.in-csv, copy.in-binary, copy.in-error, copy.out, copy.round-trip, copy.freeze) compared empty data, so their matches measured nothing. All 7 matched in each of the 4 access-method rows. Left out, citus-columnar-17 has 50 matching checks of 68 judged instead of 57 of 75 (access method 73.5 instead of 76.0), and orioledb-17 94 of 104 instead of 101 of 111 (90.4 instead of 91.0); the heap references stay at 100.
entries.cause_detail: Each COPY check packed its observation before its COPY ran, since the result list of its return statement is evaluated left to right, so the subject and its reference both recorded no steps.
entries.fix_title: Take the access-method COPY observation after the COPY runs
entries.note: v0.1.3 (45a7361f915b) was measured with the fix. The 7 checks record the COPY results of both engines there (the rows read back, COPY tags, the 22P04 of the rejected row), and all 7 match on each of the 4 access-method rows, so the scores are those of v0.1.2: citus-columnar-17 76.0 (57 of 75 judged checks matched), orioledb-17 91.0 (101 of 111), and 100 for both heap references. The other access-method checks of these rows have the same outcomes in both releases. Every row named here ran the same image digest in both releases.

entries.what: 6 COPY checks held a row to an option its reference version does not have, and were charged where the engine answered otherwise than that reference's own error: cedardb, compared with PostgreSQL 16, in pgwire.copy.in.on-error-ignore (ON_ERROR is PostgreSQL 17 and later); duckgres, compared with PostgreSQL 15, in pgwire.copy.in.default-marker (DEFAULT, 16 and later) and pgwire.copy.in.on-error-ignore; spanner-pg, compared with PostgreSQL 14, in pgwire.copy.in.csv.header-match (HEADER MATCH, 15 and later); cloudberry, compared with PostgreSQL 14, in pgwire.copy.in.csv.header and pgwire.copy.options.legacy-syntax, for the text-format HEADER case they carried (15 and later). With the fix the checks of cedardb, duckgres and spanner-pg are not applicable for a baseline older than the option. On cloudberry the text-format HEADER case moved into a check of its own, pgwire.copy.text.header, which is not applicable against PostgreSQL 14, and the two original checks now match. The binary and CSV COPY cases moved into checks of their own by the same fix charged no row of v0.1.2 again: where an engine refused binary or CSV COPY, those checks were skipped or matched.
entries.cause_detail: The checks of COPY options added in PostgreSQL 15, 16 and 17 ran against every baseline, so for an older one the reference recorded its own error and an engine was compared with that error instead of the check being left out.
entries.fix_title: Count a COPY format or option gap once, and hold no row to a newer option
entries.note: v0.1.3 (45a7361f915b) was measured with the fix. The option checks are not applicable there for a reference version older than the option: on CedarDB (PostgreSQL 16) the ON_ERROR check, on Duckgres (15) the DEFAULT and ON_ERROR checks, and on Spanner PG (14) the HEADER MATCH check. On Cloudberry (14) the text-format HEADER case moved into a check of its own, pgwire.copy.text.header, which is not applicable there, and pgwire.copy.in.csv.header and pgwire.copy.options.legacy-syntax, which carried it, match. The same rule leaves out checks that matched in v0.1.2 against a reference version without the option: HEADER MATCH, DEFAULT and ON_ERROR on Cloudberry, DEFAULT and ON_ERROR on Spanner PG. The cases the fix split into checks of their own are judged on their own: where they apply, Duckgres differs in 4, matches 1 and has 1 skipped, Cloudberry differs in 1 and matches 4, CedarDB differs in 2 and matches 1 with 4 not run after its server went down at an earlier check, and Spanner PG differs in 1 and has 2 skipped. Scores, v0.1.2 published to v0.1.3 measured (frames, types, bulk, overall): CedarDB 55.6 to 60.0, 42.8 to 62.2, 9.0 to 12.1, 38.1 to 46.6; Cloudberry 100.0 to 97.4, 99.6 to 99.8, 98.8 to 99.3, 99.5 to 98.7; Duckgres 27.8 to 32.5, 16.0 to 24.6, 14.3 to 44.7, 20.4 to 33.8; Spanner PG 13.9 to 13.2, 33.7 to 9.8, 1.2 to 7.3, 16.0 to 10.5. A v0.1.3 number also reflects the other changes between the two releases, not this fix alone: new checks (TLS and the :: cast check in frames, jsonb in types and bulk, COPY cases split into checks of their own), per-type COPY checks that compare COPY with the same engine instead of with the reference, detection fixes, and the other errata here. Every row named here ran the same image digest in both releases.

entries.what: Reproductions of pgwire findings misstated what the client sent. In 1243 of the 1530 pgwire findings, on 18 rows (all named here except alloydb-omni and spanner-pg), the message sequence listed the client's SASL or password answers during authentication as Unknown. 20 findings had no reproduction: pgwire.frame.tls.session on alloydb-omni, arcadedb, cloudberry, cratedb, doltgres, greptimedb, immudb, materialize, pgbouncer, picodata, questdb, risingwave, serenedb, spanner-pg, ydb and yugabytedb, and pgwire.frame.startup.gssenc_request on cedardb, cockroachdb, cratedb and immudb. 21 findings listed a sequence without the message the check is about: pgwire.frame.unknown_message_type on arcadedb, cedardb, clickhouse, cockroachdb, cratedb, doltgres, duckgres, greptimedb, immudb, materialize, picodata, questdb, risingwave, spanner-pg and ydb, pgwire.frame.startup.ssl_request on clickhouse, pgwire.frame.startup.gssenc_request on duckgres, picodata and ydb, and pgwire.frame.tls.scram_plus on cockroachdb and duckgres; the SSLRequest, GSSENCRequest or unknown message was left out. 15 more findings had no reproduction for a second cause: pgwire.frame.notify.listen on clickhouse, cockroachdb, cratedb, doltgres, duckgres, immudb, materialize, pgbouncer, picodata, questdb, risingwave, serenedb, spanner-pg, ydb and yugabytedb. This concerns the finding pages and vendor bundles only; the outcomes, counts and scores of every row are unaffected.
entries.cause_detail: The reproduction is derived from the frame trace. The trace records every client answer to an authentication request with the same type byte, which it names Unknown, and records the bytes our client writes directly (SSLRequest, GSSENCRequest, unknown and malformed messages) as notes, which the derivation read as part of the message before them or, at the start of a trace, dropped. Second cause: the LISTEN/NOTIFY check named its frame traces listener.txt and notifier.txt, and the export derives a reproduction only from evidence whose name says it is a trace, so it found none for that check.
entries.fix_title: Name pgwire auth answers and list raw messages in reproductions
entries.note: Not yet published; the next release is the first dataset whose reproductions are derived with the fix. The authentication answers are named by the request they answer (SASLInitialResponse, SASLResponse, PasswordMessage), and bytes our client writes directly are listed as raw followed by the bytes. The second cause is fixed by bdfd008c18485897cee70f78f8d9c3684d9105a5 Name the LISTEN/NOTIFY frame traces as traces: the check names them listener-trace.txt and notifier-trace.txt, and a524f1e946a8578624dd3048b87308745c00e7cc List the sessions of a multi-session pgwire check in the order things happened: the check's two sessions number their trace records from one counter, and the reproduction lists their messages in the order they were sent, each marked with its session. The traces in the evidence were complete in v0.1.3; only the reproductions derived from them were affected.
